body.p: The following remarks are made in response to the Action. In this Response, claims 1- 4 and 8-10 have been amended. No claims have been canceled or newly added. Claims 1-4, 6, and 8-10 are pending. The claim amendments are supported by at least, for example, paragraphs [0051] and [0052] of the Specification as filed. There is no new matter.
Claims 1-4, 6, and 8-10 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over CN 208645329 ("Pei"). Applicant traverses the rejection.
Without acquiescing to the propriety of the rejection, and to expedite prosecution, claim 1 has been amended to further recite:
a second arm link ... comprising:...
a third stage reduction assembly extending along a third axis thereof
and coupled to a second power source of the robot; and
a fourth stage reduction assembly comprising:
an input of the fourth stage reduction assembly coupled to an output of
the third stage reduction assembly; and

an output of the fourth stage reduction assembly coaxially arranged on a periphery of a second hollow shaft, wherein the output of the fourth stage reduction assembly is adapted to engage with the input of the fourth stage reduction assembly to cause a rotation of a third arm link about a fourth axis by driving the second hollow shaft to rotate about
the fourth axis.

(Emphasis added.) The Action states that Pei teaches "a first arm link (30); ... a second arm link (20) connected to the hollow shaft; a first stage reduction assembly ... and a second stage reduction assembly (23, 24, 25) comprising: an input (23) ... and an output

(25) of the second stage reduction assembly coaxially arranged on a periphery of the hollow shaft." (Action at p. 3.) Moreover, the Action states that it would have been obvious to "place a planetary gear reducer between the motor 21 and the pulley 23 ... for the benefit of increasing torque/mechanical advantage." (Action at p. 2.) For at least the following reasons, Pei does not teach the above recited features of amended claim 1.

Pei teaches a "first cantilever 20" includes a "second toothed belt transmission device comprises a driving pulley 23, a toothed belt 24 and a driven pulley 25, the driving pulley 23 is fixed on the shaft of the servo motor 21, and the driven pulley 25 is fixed on the hollow cycloid reducer 22 On [sic] the input shaft." (Pei at p. 3.) Pei also teaches that the "input shaft of the hollow cycloidal reducer 22 is driven by the servo motor 21 through the first [sic] toothed belt transmission." (Pei at p. 3.) Pei appears to teach that the "first cantilever 20" includes a "second toothed belt transmission device" that drives the "hollow cycloid reducer 22 [o]n the input shaft." Even assuming if "plac[ing] a planetary gear reducer between the motor 21 and the pulley 23" in Pei would have been obvious to a person of ordinary skill in the art (POSITA), which Applicant does not concede, Pei does not teach the "first cantilever 20" including a "third stage reduction assembly" and a "fourth stage reduction assembly," as recited in amended claim 1. Therefore, Pei does not teach that the "first cantilever 20" includes "a third stage reduction assembly extending along a third axis thereof and coupled to a second power source of the robot," and "a fourth stage reduction assembly comprising: an input of the fourth stage reduction assembly coupled to an output of the third stage reduction assembly; and an output of the fourth stage reduction assembly coaxially arranged on a periphery of a second hollow shaft," as recited in amended claim 1.

Moreover, Pei does not teach that the "first cantilever 20" includes a "fourth stage reduction assembly" to "cause a rotation of a third arm link about a fourth axis by driving the second hollow shaft to rotate about the fourth axis," as recited in amended claim 1. Instead, Pei teaches that "hanger 10" includes "a servo motor 11, a first toothed belt transmission device and a hollow cycloidal pin gear reducer 12, and the servo motor 11 and the hollow cycloid reducer 12 are mounted on the hanger 10," and that the "input shaft of the cycloid reducer 12 is driven by the servo motor 11 through the first toothed belt drive." (Pei at p. 4.) Therefore, in Pei, the "hanger 10" is driven to rotate about an axis of the "hollow cycloidal pin gear reducer 12" by the "servo motor 11" via the "first toothed belt transmission device." Thus, Pei does not teach "wherein the output of the fourth stage reduction assembly is adapted to engage with the input of the fourth stage reduction assembly to cause a rotation of a third arm link about a fourth axis by driving the second hollow shaft to rotate about the fourth axis," as recited in amended claim 1.

For at least the above reasons, independent claim 1 and its dependent claims 2- 4, 6, 8, and 9 are patentable over Pei. Although different in scope, independent claim 10 is patentable for similar reasons as claim 1. Applicant does not concede the correctness of the rejection with respect to features not discussed herein. Applicant requests favorable reconsideration of the claims and withdrawal of the rejection.

It is submitted that the rejections in the Action have been successfully traversed and that the application is now in condition for allowance. Reconsideration of the application and allowance thereof is solicited.

It is believed that all the pending claims have been addressed. However, the absence of a reply to a specific allegation or comment of the Action does not signify agreement or concession with that part. Also, the arguments herein are not exhaustive. The amendment or cancelation of a claim or other part of the Specification does not necessarily signify concession with an allegation or comment of the Action. Applicant reserves the right to prosecute the rejected claims in further prosecution of this or related applications.
